$comment: CatWrangler team-work rule book (cw:d-4664). One file, read by the Claude Code / Codex plugin hooks (lib/team-rules.mjs) and by any other client, such as the CatWrangler Harness task tool. Matching: fold typographic apostrophes to ASCII, then split the text into sentences at . ! or ? followed by whitespace, and at ; and line breaks. Compile every pattern, exception and ignore entry with new RegExp(source, flags). A sentence hits a rule when the rule applies to the surface being checked, no top-level ignore pattern matches the sentence, at least one of the rule's patterns matches, and none of its exceptions match. Each rule's examples are its test cases: every positive must hit that rule, and no negative may hit any rule on the same surface.

worker_brief.description: Instructions an agent gives a worker it starts: an Agent/Task tool prompt, or the prompt of a claude -p / codex exec command.
worker_brief.intro: CatWrangler blocked this worker launch. CatWrangler runs agents concurrently by design: every worker has its own branch, and each merge reconciles that branch against current trunk, including edits to the same file and the same lines. The brief fences or queues that work. Rewrite the sentences quoted below and launch the worker again. Naming files as starting points is fine, and so is dividing work by file.

agent_text.description: The agent's own final message for a turn.
agent_text.intro: CatWrangler: your final message holds back independent work to avoid conflicts or overlap. CatWrangler reconciles concurrent edits at merge, including edits to the same file and the same lines, so waiting buys nothing. Start that work now instead of stopping. If it really needs another task's output, say which output and carry on with everything else.

teach: CatWrangler runs agents concurrently by design: each works on its own branch, and every merge reconciles it with current trunk, even same-file, same-line edits. Splitting work by file is fine when it helps. Never fence or queue work: do not tell a worker it may not touch a file it might need, do not tell it about other workers or ask it to coordinate, do not make it wait for or start after another worker unless it needs that worker's output, do not tell it to rebase to avoid conflicts, and never hold back independent work to avoid overlap. Start it now.

rules.description: Telling a worker it may not touch or edit a file or path it might need.
rules.correction: Remove the restriction. The worker may edit any file its task needs: CatWrangler reconciles concurrent edits to the same file and lines at merge. Keep file names only as pointers, such as "start by reading X" or "the change is probably in Y".

rules.description: Telling a worker about other workers and what they are doing, or asking it to coordinate with them.
rules.correction: Remove what the brief says about other workers, and any request to coordinate with them. Each worker has its own branch, and CatWrangler raises a real conflict between decisions when it matters, so the worker needs only its own task.

rules.description: Telling a worker to wait for, or start after, another worker finishes or merges, or ordering merges between workers.
rules.correction: Launch the worker now, without waiting on or ordering it behind other workers. Keep an ordering only when this worker needs another worker's output, and name that output in the brief.

rules.description: Telling a worker to rebase, sync or re-pull to avoid conflicts with other workers.
rules.correction: Remove the rebase or sync instruction. Edit-and-merge is the default: sandbox_merge reconciles the branch against current trunk, overlaps included. Rebase only to build directly on another change.

positive: Rebase onto trunk before you start to avoid conflicts with the other workers.

negative: If you need to build directly on the new schema change, rebase with sync_branch mode rebase.
sandbox_merge reconciles your branch against current trunk, so just merge.
Pull request descriptions end with the attribution line.
Never rebase just to avoid conflicts.

rules.description: Deferring or queuing independent work to avoid overlapping files or conflicts with work in flight.
rules.correction: Start that work now, in parallel. CatWrangler reconciles concurrent edits, including edits to the same files and lines, at merge. Only a real data dependency, needing another task's output, is a reason to wait.
